props.statement: By-passing the inflowing gas partly or wholly around the heat-exchanger allows closer regulation of temperature for the final catalytic operation with maximum yield, and permits less expensive construction than the internal cooling system heretofore used.

evidence.quote: Furthermore in industrial practice « on 8. com- - mercial scale, it has been found that the portion B5 of the catalyst which first comes in contact with the gas mixture where the activity is more in- tense, may become injured by overheating or
even poisoned by impurities in the gases.
Hence it follows that the maxi- 60 mum life of a catalyst as well as maximum con- ~ version of the methanol products are largely de- pendent. upon the temperature at which such catalyst operates

props.statement: On a commercial scale, the portion of the catalyst first contacted by the gas, where the activity is more intense, may be injured by overheating or even poisoned by impurities in the gases; local overheating is likely even with cooling surfaces; maximum catalyst life and maximum conversion depend largely on the catalyst operating temperature.

props.scope: preferred operating conditions of the description
props.statement: Methanol is made from a mixture of one part carbon monoxide and two parts hydrogen by volume, preferably passed under 300 atmospheres and at a high temperature (300 to 400 °C) over a catalyst containing metallic copper and zinc oxide, with recirculation of the uncombined gases.

props.name: reaction heat insufficient without preheating the ingoing gas

evidence.quote: Under. ordinary conditions of operation the heat produced in the catalyst chamber is insufficient to maintain the reaction unless the ingoing gas mixture is pre-. 60 heated

props.statement: Under ordinary operating conditions the heat produced in the catalyst chamber is insufficient to maintain the reaction unless the ingoing gas mixture is preheated, directly or by the hot outgoing mixture through heat-exchange apparatus.

props.name: prior internal heat-transfer surfaces permit great temperature differences

evidence.quote: but such system of control inevitably permits great differ- 70 ences in temperature in various isolated parts of the catalyst mass,

props.statement: Removal of the reaction heat by heat-transfer surfaces within the catalyst mass, as heretofore practised, inevitably permits great temperature differences in isolated parts of the catalyst mass and allows no adequate temperature control for maximum conversion.

props.name: smaller first catalyst portion lets the larger portion be held at the optimum

evidence.quote: -One advantage of having the ‘upper and ini- tially-contacted. catalyst 7 of less content than the final catalyst 9, is that the temperature in the larger portion 9 of the catalyst.mass may be 105 held closely to the optimum,

props.statement: Making the initially contacted catalyst portion smaller than the final portion lets the temperature of the larger portion be held close to the optimum, since the greater part of the reaction heat is liberated in the first chamber.

props.name: success depends on temperature control in the catalyst chamber

evidence.quote: suc- cess depends almost entirely on the regulation and control of the temperatures maintained in the catalytic chamber.

props.statement: In methanol manufacture over the copper-zinc oxide catalyst, success depends almost entirely on the regulation and control of the temperatures maintained in the catalytic chamber.

props.name: deviation from optimum temperature lowers conversion; too low stops the reaction

evidence.quote: perature in either direction lowers the conver-_ sion efficiency of the catalyst with decreased yields.
It has been found that too low tempera- tures greatly decrease the activity of the catalyst,

evidence.note: 'go that' is OCR of 'so that'; '©' and 'AB' are OCR noise / a line number
evidence.quote: go that cooling takes place below that required to - maintain the reaction, and therefore production © AB of methanol ceases entirely.

props.statement: Variation of the catalyst temperature in either direction from the optimum lowers the conversion efficiency and the yield; too low temperatures greatly decrease the activity of the catalyst, so that the reaction cannot be maintained and methanol production ceases entirely.

props.name: zoned temperature control by admitting cooler gas

evidence.quote: According to my invention I contro] the tem- — perature throughout the catalyst mass in varying __ sections or zones
since the greater part of the heat generated through the reaction is liberated in the lesser portion of the catalyst mass which ini- tially comes in contact with the gas mixture
The temperature control may be attained by passing comparatively cool gas at various points within the converter to. be circulated therein.

props.statement: The temperature is controlled in separate sections or zones of the catalyst mass: the greater part of the reaction heat is liberated in the lesser, initially contacted portion, so the major, last-reached portion can be held close to the optimum temperature for maximum methanol conversion by admitting comparatively cool gas at various points and by by-passing the heat-exchanger.
